<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
**⚠️ Warning: The availability gate failed.**

- **Failed gate:** Availability was **99.1%**, below the 99.5% threshold by **0.4 percentage points**.
- **Passed gate:** The longest incident lasted 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the 60-minute limit.

---

**Weekly Availability Summary**

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ Failed (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Passed (19 min margin) |
| Incident count | 2 | — | — |
| Total incident duration | 53 min (12 + 41) | — | — |

**Note on a possible discrepancy:** Over a full 24/7 week (10,080 minutes), 99.1% availability means about **91 minutes** of downtime. The two logged incidents total only **53 minutes**, which would give about 99.47%. That leaves roughly **38 minutes of downtime unexplained** by the incident log. Possible causes include unlogged incidents, planned maintenance counted against availability, partial degradations, or a measurement window other than 24/7. It's worth reconciling, because even the 53 logged minutes alone exceed the roughly 50 minutes of downtime that the 99.5% gate allows.
